reported.title: Relay run length collapses because drive() re-evaluates the hold switch every loop
reported.description: drive() at lines 46-47 recomputes the relay output from `running && !held()` on every loop iteration, so any read of D3 as LOW (bounce, chatter, or a floating input) immediately forces D6 LOW mid-run instead of letting the 2000 ms run complete. The measured evidence shows pulses of 514 ms, 67 ms, 46 ms and 201 ms instead of 2000 ± 150 ms, and missed starts such as "D6 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 5.20 s". The run timer in startRun() (lines 29-30) is correct, but the output is gated by an unsynchronised input read rather than by the scheduled state. D6 missed 2 of 11 trigger(s): D6 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 6.21 s. 25 of 25 pulse(s) had the wrong length: pulse from 5.00 s lasted 514 ms, expected 2000 ± 150 ms.

reported.title: No debounce or state latching on D3 causes relay chatter far above the 2-toggle limit
reported.description: held() at lines 39-42 reads the raw pin with no debounce, and drive() at lines 46-47 writes D6 on every loop pass, so each bounce edge on D3 toggles the relay directly. The measurements show 16 toggles in a 5000 ms window for button bounce, 6 for hold-then-release, and 28 for rapid chatter around the start, all against a limit of 2. Because the relay output is derived combinationally from the input rather than from a latched run state, contact chatter and mid-run release both produce extra transitions. D6 toggled 16 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 5.00 s (limit 2), and 16 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

truth.description: The 16-bit clock is compared with absolute deadlines, so the schedule breaks whenever the clock wraps, every 65.5 s of uptime

exposing_checks.behaviour: serial lines matching '^mix \\d+$' every 5000 ms (A run starts every 5 s)
D6 must not toggle more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window (Mixer switching rate)

judge_input.spec:
- Mixer relay on D6; hold switch on D3 with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Run the mixer (D6 HIGH) for 2000 ms out of every 5000 ms, the first run starting 5000 ms after power-up.
- Print `mix <n>` when each run starts, once per 5000 ms ±250 ms.
- While D3 is held LOW, keep D6 LOW. The runs are still counted and printed.
- The mixer must not change state more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window.
